lessons.title: What Is Artificial Intelligence?
lessons.description: Distinguish learned prediction from fixed rules and human judgment. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Distinguish learned prediction from fixed rules and human judgment.

measurable_outcomes.text: Distinguish learned prediction from fixed rules and human judgment.
Classify six campus tasks as fixed-rule, model-assisted or human-led. Give an input, expected output and error consequence for each.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: Every automated process is AI, and using AI necessarily improves it.

key_concepts.name: What Is Artificial Intelligence?
key_concepts.explanation: An AI system uses a model to perform a task such as classifying an input or generating a response. A fixed rule follows an explicitly written condition; a learned model derives patterns from examples. Neither arrangement guarantees a correct decision. Start with the task, the available evidence and the cost of an error before deciding whether AI is useful.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A campus room booking limit can be enforced by a fixed capacity rule. Classifying free-text maintenance requests may benefit from a trained model, but uncertain cases still need a person. Choose the rule for capacity because its decision criterion is explicit.

lessons.title: How Machine Learning Works
lessons.description: Explain training, held-out evaluation and generalization. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Explain training, held-out evaluation and generalization.

measurable_outcomes.text: Explain training, held-out evaluation and generalization.
Partition twelve fictional messages into training and evaluation sets. Identify a duplicate and explain how it would distort the result.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: Perfect training accuracy proves the model will work on new inputs.

key_concepts.name: How Machine Learning Works
key_concepts.explanation: Machine learning fits a model using examples and an objective. Training performance measures fit to those examples, not performance on unseen cases. Keep evaluation examples separate so you can detect memorization and overfitting. Check whether the evaluation population resembles the population where the model will operate; a good score on an unsuitable sample is weak evidence.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A request classifier learns from 80 labeled messages and is evaluated on 20 unused messages. If duplicate messages occur in both sets, the result exaggerates generalization. Remove duplicates before splitting and report the split method.

lessons.title: Generative AI
lessons.description: Separate generated content from evidence supporting its claims. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Separate generated content from evidence supporting its claims.

measurable_outcomes.text: Separate generated content from evidence supporting its claims.
Draft a fictional event announcement, annotate every factual claim against a supplied brief and correct unsupported details.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: A fluent generated answer is automatically factual.

key_concepts.name: Generative AI
key_concepts.explanation: Generative models produce new text, images or other outputs from learned patterns and supplied context. A plausible output is not a retrieved fact or a guarantee of originality. Use generation to propose drafts, then verify factual claims, permissions and task constraints. Record what the tool contributed so another person can understand how the final artifact was produced.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary

lessons.title: Large Language Models
lessons.description: Explain next-token generation without treating it as a truth test. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Explain next-token generation without treating it as a truth test.

measurable_outcomes.text: Explain next-token generation without treating it as a truth test.
Compare two different answers to a fictional notice question. Mark factual differences and define the evidence needed to resolve them.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: The most confident continuation must be the correct one.

key_concepts.name: Large Language Models
key_concepts.explanation: A language model estimates possible continuations from its context and learned parameters. Repeated generation may produce different wording or conclusions. Instruction following and apparent reasoning can be useful, but neither establishes that a factual claim is supported. Evaluate the answer against the task and evidence rather than attributing human understanding or certainty to the model.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary

lessons.title: Tokens, Context & Model Behavior
lessons.description: Identify information lost through context limits and ambiguous instructions. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Identify information lost through context limits and ambiguous instructions.

measurable_outcomes.text: Identify information lost through context limits and ambiguous instructions.
Compress a fictional project brief to five sentences while retaining owner, deadline, budget status and exclusions. Compare both versions field by field.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: Anything mentioned earlier is permanently available to the model.

key_concepts.name: Tokens, Context & Model Behavior
key_concepts.explanation: Models process units called tokens, which need not correspond to whole words. The context contains instructions, input and prior conversation within a finite budget. Information outside that context may be unavailable to the model. Put critical constraints where they can be retained, summarize carefully and check that summaries preserve decision-relevant details. A longer prompt can still contain conflicting instructions.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A long meeting summary omits that a budget is provisional. The next request treats it as approved. Restore the approval status explicitly and verify the revised output preserves it.

lessons.title: Training, Inference & Fine-Tuning
lessons.description: Choose between prompting, retrieval and fine-tuning for a stated need. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Choose between prompting, retrieval and fine-tuning for a stated need.

measurable_outcomes.text: Choose between prompting, retrieval and fine-tuning for a stated need.
Choose an approach for current notices, consistent writing style and a fixed arithmetic rule. Explain what changes and how you would evaluate it.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: Uploading a document into a conversation necessarily retrains the model.

key_concepts.name: Training, Inference & Fine-Tuning
key_concepts.explanation: Training adjusts model parameters; inference uses parameters to produce an output. Fine-tuning continues training on a selected dataset to alter behavior. Supplying a document in context does not itself fine-tune the model. For changing factual material, retrieval may be more appropriate than changing parameters. Any approach needs evaluation, access controls and a plan for incorrect outputs.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: University deadlines change each term. Retrieve the current approved notice instead of fine-tuning solely to memorize dates. Fine-tuning might address a consistent formatting task, but it does not remove the need to check dates.

lessons.title: AI Models & Model Selection
lessons.description: Evaluate candidate tools using task-specific quality and operational constraints. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Evaluate candidate tools using task-specific quality and operational constraints.

measurable_outcomes.text: Evaluate candidate tools using task-specific quality and operational constraints.
Create a comparison sheet for two hypothetical tools using five notice-summary cases and explicit acceptance criteria.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: The largest or most popular model is always the best choice.

key_concepts.name: AI Models & Model Selection
key_concepts.explanation: Model selection is a decision about fitness for a task. Define representative inputs and observable quality criteria before comparing candidates. Include privacy, latency, cost, accessibility and failure recovery alongside answer quality. Run the same cases under comparable conditions and record versions when known. A small evaluation supports a bounded conclusion, not a universal ranking.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: For summarizing public notices, one tool is faster but omits eligibility conditions. A rubric that requires accurate eligibility should reject those outputs even if users prefer their style. Report both latency and failed conditions.

key_concepts.name: Multimodal AI
key_concepts.explanation: Multimodal systems accept or generate more than one media type. Images can contain unreadable text, ambiguous scales or cropped context; audio can contain uncertain names or overlapping speakers. learning_objective.text: Trace a retrieved answer through source selection, access and claim verification.

key_concepts.name: RAG & Knowledge Grounding
key_concepts.explanation: Retrieval-augmented generation selects source material and supplies it to a model. Retrieval can improve access to relevant information, but irrelevant, stale or malicious material can still enter the context. Apply access controls before retrieval, preserve source references and verify that each claim follows from a source. If no supporting passage exists, report the gap rather than invent an answer.

Communicate uncertainty in terms of what action should wait for verification.

key_concepts.name: Responsible AI
key_concepts.explanation: Responsible use requires considering who supplies data, who is affected and who can correct a mistake. Give a named person responsibility for consequential decisions and preserve a route to question or revise the outcome.

key_concepts.name: AI as a Productivity Tool

key_concepts.explanation: A useful prompt states a goal, relevant input and an observable standard for success. key_concepts.name: Instructions, Context & Constraints
key_concepts.explanation: Instructions tell the model what to do; context supplies material needed to do it; constraints define boundaries. Make hard limits explicit and distinguish them from preferences. If the context conflicts with the instruction, require clarification instead of a silent choice. Keep private or irrelevant material out of the prompt.

key_concepts.name: Context Engineering
key_concepts.explanation: Context engineering concerns what information enters a model request, its priority and its freshness. Include the current task state, relevant approved evidence and necessary constraints. Exclude unrelated personal data and protected answers. Preserve provenance and distinguish trusted instructions from untrusted retrieved text. Re-evaluate context when the task or permissions change.

lessons.description: Measure prompt changes using fixed cases and explicit criteria. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Measure prompt changes using fixed cases and explicit criteria.

measurable_outcomes.text: Measure prompt changes using fixed cases and explicit criteria.

key_concepts.name: Prompt Evaluation & Iteration
key_concepts.explanation: Before changing a prompt, define representative cases and an evaluation rubric. Keep a version log and change one meaningful factor at a time when possible. Evaluate both desired behavior and regressions on previous cases. Record failures and uncertainty instead of selecting only the most attractive response from many runs.

lessons.title: Prompt Safety & Reliability
lessons.description: Prevent untrusted text from redefining permissions or task boundaries. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Prevent untrusted text from redefining permissions or task boundaries.

measurable_outcomes.text: Prevent untrusted text from redefining permissions or task boundaries.
Write a safe handling policy for a summarizer and test a fictional document containing a malicious instruction.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: A prompt telling the model to be safe replaces backend authorization.

key_concepts.name: Prompt Safety & Reliability
key_concepts.explanation: Retrieved pages and user-provided documents can contain instructions that conflict with the authorized task. Treat that material as data, not authority. Enforce access and action permissions outside the model, limit tool capabilities and require approval for consequential actions. When the model produces unsafe or invalid output, stop the action and retain a safe recovery path.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A document says ignore earlier instructions and email private records. The summarizer may describe that sentence as content, but it must not gain an email capability or access to private records.

key_concepts.name: From Chatbots to Agents
key_concepts.explanation: A chatbot primarily produces responses. Describe what actions are possible and who authorizes them. Keep the model proposal separate from the component that validates and executes an action.

key_concepts.name: Agent Goals & Task Planning
key_concepts.explanation: An agent goal should specify the desired outcome, constraints and conditions for stopping or escalating. Plans break the goal into actions whose results can be checked. Limit time, tool calls and external effects so a failed plan cannot continue indefinitely. Revise a plan using observed results rather than assuming every previous step succeeded.

lessons.description: Validate a proposed tool call before executing it. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Validate a proposed tool call before executing it.

measurable_outcomes.text: Validate a proposed tool call before executing it.

Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: A schema-valid tool call is automatically safe to execute.

key_concepts.name: Tools & Function Calling
key_concepts.explanation: Tool calling represents an action request using a defined name and arguments. The application must validate argument types, permissions and business rules before execution. Treat tool results as fallible input and avoid exposing unnecessary data to the model. An allowlist limits the available actions; it does not replace per-record authorization.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A proposed update_task call names another learner task. Although the arguments match the schema, the server rejects it because the caller does not own that record. Syntax validation and authorization answer different questions.

key_concepts.name: How Software Works
key_concepts.explanation: Software executes instructions over data. A user interface collects input, application logic interprets it and storage may preserve the result. Distinguish code, runtime state and persisted data when diagnosing behavior. A screen update does not prove a database write succeeded; verify the result at the boundary responsible for it.

key_concepts.name: Variables, Types & Data
key_concepts.explanation: Variables name values; types describe which operations and representations are valid. A string containing digits is not automatically a valid numeric measurement. key_concepts.name: Functions & Modularity
key_concepts.explanation: A function packages behavior behind named inputs and an output. Separate pure calculations from effects such as database writes so each can be checked independently. State preconditions and error behavior, and avoid hidden dependencies on unrelated global state. Modularity helps when boundaries reflect responsibilities rather than arbitrary file size.

key_concepts.name: Web Fundamentals
key_concepts.explanation: A browser requests resources from a server. HTML provides document structure, CSS presentation and JavaScript interactive behavior. URLs identify resources, while HTTP requests and responses carry method, status, headers and optional bodies. Network failures and server errors are normal possibilities, so an interactive page needs visible loading and failure states.

key_concepts.name: Backend Fundamentals

key_concepts.name: What Is Cloud Computing?
key_concepts.explanation: Cloud computing provides computing resources through a service rather than requiring the application team to own every machine. Service models divide operational responsibilities differently, but the application owner still needs to manage data, access and configuration. Evaluate the required capability, reliability and cost instead of assuming cloud hosting removes operational work.

learning_objective.text: Design stateless execution with external durable state.

key_concepts.name: Serverless & Modern Deployment
key_concepts.explanation: Serverless execution runs code on demand under platform-defined limits. Do not assume one process will retain memory, local files or a long-running connection between requests. Persist durable state outside the invocation, make retries safe and account for time limits. Deployment configuration should describe required environment values without containing their secret contents.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A function stores processed submission IDs in memory. A new instance loses that set and processes a retry twice. Move deduplication into a database uniqueness rule or durable idempotency record.

Deployment configuration should describe required environment values without containing their secret contents.

key_concepts.name: Identity, Secrets & Configuration
key_concepts.explanation: Configuration describes how an application connects to its environment. Some values are public identifiers; others grant authority and must remain secret. Store secrets in an approved secret mechanism, restrict access and rotate exposed credentials. Use different identities for development and production where practical, and never treat hiding a value in frontend code as protection.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary

key_concepts.name: Reliability, Scaling & Observability
key_concepts.explanation: Reliability concerns whether users can complete the intended task, not just whether a process is running. Measure errors, latency and critical workflow outcomes with safe logs and correlation identifiers. Scaling adds capacity but may expose shared-state or database bottlenecks. Define alerts, ownership and recovery procedures that correspond to actual user impact.

key_concepts.name: Identity & Authentication
key_concepts.explanation: Authentication establishes which identity is making a request, using a mechanism such as a credential or an existing session. Protect credentials, validate sessions server-side and handle expiry and revocation. Authentication does not decide which records the person may access. Error handling should avoid exposing unnecessary account information.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A user remains on an open page after their session expires. The next save must revalidate the session and ask them to sign in, preserving unsaved work safely rather than trusting the old UI state.

key_concepts.name: Data Privacy & Protection
key_concepts.explanation: Privacy work begins by asking whether a data item is needed at all. State the purpose, who may access it and when it should be deleted or reviewed. Protect data in transit and storage, but recognize that encryption does not justify unnecessary collection. Use applicable institutional policy and qualified guidance for legal requirements.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A study planner needs available hours, not a government identity number. Remove the unnecessary field and define a retention period for obsolete schedules rather than keeping every record indefinitely.

key_concepts.name: Social Engineering & Human Risk
key_concepts.explanation: Social engineering manipulates trust, urgency or authority to obtain information or actions. Pause when a request seeks credentials, unusual payments or bypassed procedures. Verify through a known independent channel rather than the contact supplied in the suspicious message. Report the event and preserve useful evidence without spreading sensitive material.

lessons.description: Contain untrusted model inputs and outputs within existing access boundaries. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

measurable_outcomes.text: Contain untrusted model inputs and outputs within existing access boundaries.

key_concepts.name: AI Security
key_concepts.explanation: AI systems introduce risks such as malicious instructions in retrieved content, excessive tool authority and leakage through prompts or logs. Treat model output as untrusted until validated. Filter authorized context before calling the model and enforce tool permissions outside it. Test conceptual attacks in a controlled fixture without exposing real secrets.

Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: A high overall accuracy score proves a system is fair.

key_concepts.name: Responsible AI & Bias
key_concepts.explanation: Bias can arise from collection, labels, objectives and how outputs are used. Examine whether relevant groups are represented and whether errors have unequal consequences. Avoid treating one aggregate metric as a complete fairness assessment. Include affected people in review where appropriate and provide a process to challenge or correct outcomes.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A recommendation system performs well overall but repeatedly excludes students with limited connectivity. Inspect group-specific outcomes and the input assumptions instead of relying solely on the overall score.

key_concepts.name: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
key_concepts.explanation: Problem solving begins by stating the observed behavior and the expected behavior. key_concepts.name: Problems Worth Solving
key_concepts.explanation: A product idea should start with a specific person, situation and recurring difficulty. Separate direct observations from assumptions about causes or willingness to pay. lessons.title: Customer Discovery
lessons.description: Ask about real behavior without leading participants toward your idea. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Ask about real behavior without leading participants toward your idea.

measurable_outcomes.text: Ask about real behavior without leading participants toward your idea.

Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: Positive reactions to a pitch prove demand.

key_concepts.name: Customer Discovery
key_concepts.explanation: Discovery interviews seek evidence about existing behavior, constraints and priorities. Ask open questions about recent experiences rather than asking whether someone likes your proposed solution. Obtain appropriate consent, minimize personal data and distinguish quotations from interpretations. A small interview sample provides leads and uncertainty, not proof of a whole market.

lessons.title: Evaluating Ideas
lessons.description: Compare ideas using evidence, risk and testability. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Compare ideas using evidence, risk and testability.

measurable_outcomes.text: Compare ideas using evidence, risk and testability.
Compare two fictional ideas, identify the highest-risk assumption for each and design a discriminating experiment.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: A high score in an idea matrix proves the business will succeed.

key_concepts.name: Evaluating Ideas
key_concepts.explanation: Evaluate an idea by the importance of the problem, who experiences it, existing alternatives and the hardest assumptions. Separate evidence from confidence and choose a low-cost test of the riskiest claim. Feasibility, desirability and sustainability are different questions. A scoring table helps organize judgment but does not turn guesses into facts.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary

lessons.title: Value Proposition
lessons.description: State a concrete user benefit relative to an existing alternative. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: State a concrete user benefit relative to an existing alternative.

measurable_outcomes.text: State a concrete user benefit relative to an existing alternative.
Write a value proposition for a fictional room-coordination service with target user, alternative, benefit and a measurable test.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: A list of product features is the same as a user value proposition.

key_concepts.name: Value Proposition
key_concepts.explanation: A value proposition connects a specific user problem to a benefit the user can recognize. Explain the alternative currently used and why the proposed change could be better. Avoid vague claims such as smarter or revolutionary. Define a measurable outcome and test whether users value it enough to change behavior.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: Find an available room without messaging five groups is more concrete than AI-powered campus innovation. Test whether the proposed process actually reduces unsuccessful searches.

lessons.title: Business Models
lessons.description: Explain who benefits, who pays and which costs recur. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Explain who benefits, who pays and which costs recur.

measurable_outcomes.text: Explain who benefits, who pays and which costs recur.
Build a fictional unit-economics worksheet with payer, price, fixed costs, variable costs and a sensitivity check.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: Growing user numbers always improve financial sustainability.

key_concepts.name: Business Models
key_concepts.explanation: A business model describes how value is delivered and sustained. Identify the user, payer, distribution route and recurring costs, which may be different from initial build costs. Use explicit assumptions and simple calculations before projecting growth. Do not present fictional revenue or demand as measured results.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A service earns a fictional 100 units per month but costs 120 units to operate. More users may worsen the loss if costs scale faster than revenue. Separate fixed and per-user costs before extrapolating.

lessons.description: Choose the smallest experiment that tests a consequential assumption. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Choose the smallest experiment that tests a consequential assumption.

measurable_outcomes.text: Choose the smallest experiment that tests a consequential assumption.

Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: An MVP must contain every major feature of the eventual product.

key_concepts.name: Building an MVP
key_concepts.explanation: A minimum viable product is a bounded way to learn about a value proposition, not a license to ignore safety or quality. Select the assumption to test and include only the capabilities needed for that test. Define a success threshold, protect participant data and state what the prototype cannot do. A manual service may test demand before software is necessary.

lessons.title: Testing, Feedback & Iteration
lessons.description: Use observed behavior to decide whether to change, continue or stop. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Use observed behavior to decide whether to change, continue or stop.

measurable_outcomes.text: Use observed behavior to decide whether to change, continue or stop.

Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: Positive feedback is equivalent to demonstrated adoption.

key_concepts.name: Testing, Feedback & Iteration
key_concepts.explanation: An experiment needs a question, procedure and decision rule. Observe actual behavior and record negative feedback as well as positive reactions. Compare results with the original threshold instead of redefining success afterward. Choose the next change based on the evidence and preserve a record of what was learned.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A booking prototype gets compliments but only one of ten participants completes a booking. Investigate the failed steps and value assumption rather than counting compliments as adoption.

lessons.title: What Is Vibe Coding?
lessons.description: Explain the developer responsibility for understanding and verifying AI-generated changes. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Explain the developer responsibility for understanding and verifying AI-generated changes.

measurable_outcomes.text: Explain the developer responsibility for understanding and verifying AI-generated changes.
Review a small generated task-counter proposal. Explain its behavior, identify a boundary case and record an independent verification result.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: A coding agent completion message is sufficient evidence that the feature works.

key_concepts.name: What Is Vibe Coding?
key_concepts.explanation: AI-assisted development uses a coding assistant to propose or implement software changes. The developer remains responsible for requirements, architecture, access boundaries and the observed behavior of the result. Start with a small task, inspect the proposed code and compare it with acceptance criteria. A generated explanation or completion claim is not execution evidence. Preserve a manual path when the assistant is unavailable and disclose assistance honestly.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: An agent implements a task counter and says tests pass, but provides no run output. Inspect the diff, execute a test with zero and multiple tasks and record the actual result. If the counter includes deleted tasks, reject the completion claim and investigate the query.

lessons.title: Idea → Build Specification
lessons.description: Convert an idea into bounded requirements, data rules and acceptance criteria. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Convert an idea into bounded requirements, data rules and acceptance criteria.

measurable_outcomes.text: Convert an idea into bounded requirements, data rules and acceptance criteria.

key_concepts.name: Idea → Build Specification
key_concepts.explanation: A build specification states the user, desired outcome, inputs, observable behavior and exclusions. Include unhappy paths and data ownership rather than describing only a screen. Separate required behavior from optional polish and identify unresolved decisions before coding. The specification should let a reviewer decide whether a change meets the need without guessing what the author intended.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: For a study-task organizer, require an owner-scoped task list, nonempty titles and persistence after reload. Exclude shared tasks from the first version. Acceptance includes rejecting another user update and showing a failed-save message without losing input.

learning_objective.text: Give a coding agent bounded scope, relevant context and verification obligations.

measurable_outcomes.text: Give a coding agent bounded scope, relevant context and verification obligations.

key_concepts.name: Prompting Coding Agents
key_concepts.explanation: An agent brief should identify the outcome, constraints, repository entry points and tests that demonstrate success. Ask the agent to inspect existing code before choosing changes and to preserve established architecture unless the task requires otherwise. Specify stop conditions for missing information or unsafe effects. Require a diff summary and actual validation results, keeping secrets out of prompts and logs.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A request to fix task validation names the current form, server command and database constraint. It asks for the smallest change and tests for empty and whitespace-only titles. It does not authorize replacing authentication or deploying the app.

key_concepts.name: Backend, Database & APIs
key_concepts.explanation: Backend changes must validate untrusted input and derive identity from the authenticated session. Use canonical service boundaries and database constraints rather than inventing a parallel write path. Prefer additive migrations, inspect row-level policies and verify cross-user denial. Keep secrets server-side and define request, response and error contracts so the UI can recover correctly.

key_concepts.name: Debugging With AI
key_concepts.explanation: Give the assistant the expected behavior, actual behavior, minimal reproduction and relevant safe logs. Form hypotheses and inspect the responsible state before editing. Avoid repeated speculative rewrites, and remove temporary diagnostics that expose unnecessary information.

key_concepts.name: Git/GitHub for AI Development
key_concepts.explanation: Inspect repository status before work, keep unrelated changes intact and use a focused branch for a bounded task. key_concepts.name: Testing & E2E Verification
key_concepts.explanation: Unit tests check focused logic, integration tests check boundaries and browser tests check a user journey. lessons.description: Review generated changes for secrets, permissions and unsafe trust assumptions. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying practice.

learning_objective.text: Review generated changes for secrets, permissions and unsafe trust assumptions.

measurable_outcomes.text: Review generated changes for secrets, permissions and unsafe trust assumptions.

Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: A workaround that makes the feature pass is acceptable even if it bypasses authorization.

key_concepts.name: Security & Responsible Vibe Coding
key_concepts.explanation: Generated code can introduce excessive privileges, unsafe input handling or accidental secret exposure. Inspect the diff at trust boundaries and test authorization outside the UI. Use only authorized test accounts and synthetic data, avoid posting credentials to an assistant and rotate any credential that was exposed. Human responsibility includes understanding why a mitigation works and reporting residual risk.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A generated client component embeds an administrative key to bypass a failed query. Remove the privileged client path, rotate any exposed key and repair the authorized server/database path. Passing the query is not worth removing the access boundary.

lessons.title: Production Application Capstone
lessons.description: Deliver and explain an AI-assisted application with independently checkable release evidence. Produce and defend the result of the accompanying project.

learning_objective.text: Deliver and explain an AI-assisted application with independently checkable release evidence.

measurable_outcomes.text: Deliver and explain an AI-assisted application with independently checkable release evidence.

Submit requirements, architecture decisions, implementation, repository and Git history, working UI, applicable backend/data, tests, security checks, deployment, E2E evidence, README and a reflection distinguishing agent output from your verification.
Explain why this misconception is unsafe or incorrect: A production-oriented capstone can claim deployment or security verification without executing those checks.

key_concepts.name: Production Application Capstone
key_concepts.explanation: The capstone joins requirements, architecture, implementation and operations into one reviewable delivery. Keep agent work bounded and record your own technical decisions. Demonstrate a working UI and backend/data path where applicable, focused Git history, unit/integration/browser tests, security checks and an actual authorized deployment. Include health observations, recovery instructions, a README and reflection on errors caught. Unexecuted checks or an undeployed prototype cannot be described as a production release.

key_concepts.name: Decision boundary
key_concepts.explanation: A study-task application is deployed to a test environment, tested through creation and reload, and checked with two users for isolation. A release report links the exact commit, test outputs, deployment, README and rollback procedure. An unresolved security failure blocks approval even if the UI works.

instructional_content.text: The capstone joins requirements, architecture, implementation and operations into one reviewable delivery. Keep agent work bounded and record your own technical decisions. Demonstrate a working UI and backend/data path where applicable, focused Git history, unit/integration/browser tests, security checks and an actual authorized deployment. Include health observations, recovery instructions, a README and reflection on errors caught. Unexecuted checks or an undeployed prototype cannot be described as a production release.

instructional_content.heading: Apply it to a concrete case
instructional_content.text: A study-task application is deployed to a test environment, tested through creation and reload, and checked with two users for isolation. A release report links the exact commit, test outputs, deployment, README and rollback procedure. An unresolved security failure blocks approval even if the UI works.

instructional_content.heading: Inspect the result
instructional_content.text: Use the method above on the practice task. Record the input, your decision, its supporting reason and the actual result of a check. Explain how your result avoids this mistake: A production-oriented capstone can claim deployment or security verification without executing those checks. A plan or generated claim is not evidence that a check ran.

projects.problem: Justify an AI solution and its boundaries using reproducible evidence.
requirements: Deliver a notice-assistant proposal, three evaluated examples, a failure log, responsible-use review and a five-minute explanation of limitations.
Demonstrate the stated objective using inspectable artifacts and recorded checks.
Do not claim unexecuted work as completed.
deliverables: Deliver a notice-assistant proposal, three evaluated examples, a failure log, responsible-use review and a five-minute explanation of limitations.

rubric.criterion: Explain and correctly apply: Justify an AI solution and its boundaries using reproducible evidence.
anchors: No relevant explanation
Repeats terms without applying them
Partly correct with a material conceptual error
Correct explanation applied to the case
Correct application plus a justified boundary or counterexample

rubric.criterion: Deliver the requested work: Deliver a notice-assistant proposal, three evaluated examples, a failure log, responsible-use review and a five-minute explanation of limitations.
anchors: No artifact
Unrelated artifact
Partially completed or not inspectable
Complete artifact with traceable inputs and output
Complete reproducible artifact with clear reasoning and documented revisions

rubric.criterion: Check the lesson-specific failure illustrated here: A polished demo proves a solution is reliable in all circumstances.
anchors: No check
Unsupported claim that it works
A check is described but its outcome is not recorded
A relevant check was executed and its actual outcome recorded
Normal and boundary checks recorded with limitations and a root-cause explanation

rubric.criterion: Identify your contribution, sources, AI assistance, synthetic inputs and unexecuted work accurately; use only authorized data and test systems.
anchors: Fabricated evidence or unauthorized activity
Missing provenance
Incomplete disclosure or ambiguous execution claims
Accurate provenance and disclosure with no unresolved authorization issue
Accurate provenance plus a clear audit trail and appropriate privacy minimization

artifacts.file_policy: existing file_objects ownership and authorized storage checks

standard: Distinguish learned prediction from fixed rules and human judgment.
Explain training, held-out evaluation and generalization.
Separate generated content from evidence supporting its claims.
Explain next-token generation without treating it as a truth test.
Identify information lost through context limits and ambiguous instructions.
